title: ERC-8262 provider discovery document
description: Served at GET https://{trustDomainId}/.well-known/erc8262-provider.json (SPEC.md section 10.3). Discovery is never a pin: the consumer's allowlist pins the trust domain to its attestor, and every key and root is checked against the Oracle deployment named in the evidence. Re-fetch at least every revocationCheckSeconds; updatedAt never decreases. Body at most 65536 bytes.

protocolVersion.description: Provider protocol version; equals the `/v{n}/erc8262/` path segment. A consumer MUST refuse a version it does not implement.

trustDomainId.description: The independently controlled signing domain: the lowercase DNS host that serves this provider's discovery document and evidence endpoint. A document is authoritative only when fetched over https, without redirects, from this exact host. The host proves nothing about the attestor: the consumer's allowlist pins each trust domain to its attestorProviderId per Oracle deployment, and a host it does not list is refused.

mode.description: `native`: the source operates its own keys, so the trust domain is the source's and lists exactly one source. `gateway`: an operator re-signs one or more vendor sources under one key set; every source behind it shares this one trust domain.

operator.description: Human-readable name of the party controlling the keys.

items.description: An ERC-8262 Oracle deployment and this trust domain's attestor on it. chainId and oracleAddress bind every artifact to one deployment (ERC-8262 signed payloads and credential roots are deployment-scoped), so evidence for one chain or Oracle is never accepted on another.

attestorProviderId.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256, nonzero) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

deployments.description: One entry per Oracle deployment. A (chainId, oracleAddress) pair MUST appear at most once (a consumer refuses a duplicate): one trust domain maps to one attestor per deployment.

items.description: A signing key of this trust domain. Rotation: publish the successor with notBefore at the rotation instant, then set the predecessor's notAfter and update the Oracle (setCredentialSigner; registerSignerPubkeyHash plus revokeSignerPubkeyHash of the predecessor) in the same change. The Oracle registry is authoritative over this list. A key never issues before the Oracle holds it.

keyId.description: Provider-chosen key identifier, unique within the trust domain and never reused.

use.description: Signs EIP-712 CredentialRootPublication for proof type 4 roots.

credentialSigner.description: The address the Oracle MUST hold as getCredentialSigner(attestorProviderId) while this key is current (no notAfter); a consumer refuses evidence naming a current key whose credentialSigner differs. Not checked once retired: the Oracle then holds the successor.

notBefore.description: Unix seconds; first instant the key may issue.

notAfter.description: Unix seconds, exclusive; set when the key is retired by rotation. Evidence claiming an issuedAt at or after it is refused. A retired credential-root key's evidence stays valid until its own expiresAt (its roots stay registered). A retired signed-signals key ends at notAfter: proof types 7-9 are signed per proof, so evidence naming it is refused from then on and the provider revokes its hash on-chain in the same change.

revokedAt.description: Unix seconds; set when the key is revoked (compromise). Revocation is retroactive: every evidence naming this key is refused whatever its issuedAt, because a compromised key can backdate. Never cleared, and a consumer remembers it per (trustDomainId, keyId): a later document omitting it does not restore the key.

keyId.description: Provider-chosen key identifier, unique within the trust domain and never reused.

use.description: Signs signal payloads for proof types 7, 8 and 9.

signerPubkeyHash.description: The hash registered on the Oracle (signerProvider(hash) == attestorProviderId).

notBefore.description: Unix seconds; first instant the key may issue.

notAfter.description: Unix seconds, exclusive; set when the key is retired by rotation. Evidence claiming an issuedAt at or after it is refused. A retired credential-root key's evidence stays valid until its own expiresAt (its roots stay registered). A retired signed-signals key ends at notAfter: proof types 7-9 are signed per proof, so evidence naming it is refused from then on and the provider revokes its hash on-chain in the same change.

revokedAt.description: Unix seconds; set when the key is revoked (compromise). Revocation is retroactive: every evidence naming this key is refused whatever its issuedAt, because a compromised key can backdate. Never cleared, and a consumer remembers it per (trustDomainId, keyId): a later document omitting it does not restore the key.

keys.description: keyId MUST be unique within the document (a consumer refuses a duplicate).

sources.description: sourceId MUST be unique within the document (a consumer refuses a duplicate).

sourceId.description: The commercial evidence source (the vendor whose check produced the claim), e.g. `sumsub`. The same sourceId may appear under several trust domains (a vendor reached natively and through a gateway); quorum never counts sourceIds.

claimType.description: The claim, namespaced `<namespace>.<name>`, e.g. `kyc.individual`, `personhood.unique`. Consumers map (sourceId, claimType) to their own scoring policy; a provider never sends points, categories or tiers.

policyId.description: The provider's verification policy under which the claim was established (e.g. a KYC level). Immutable per id: a change in what the provider checks is a new policyId, never an edit. Distinct from the consumer's scoring policy version, which a provider never sends.

proofType.description: The ERC-8262 proof type the claim feeds: 4 (ATTESTATION, credential-root inclusion), 7 (COMPLIANCE_SIGNED), 8 (RISK_SCORE_SIGNED) or 9 (COMPLIANCE_MULTI_SIGNED).

revocationCheckSeconds.description: Revocation: the longest a consumer may rely on a fetched evidence status (and this document) without re-fetching. A 410 for a held evidenceId means revoked; any other non-200 response means unavailable, never revoked.

updatedAt.description: Unix seconds of the last change to this document. Never decreases: a consumer refuses a document older than one it has observed for the same trust domain (a stale cache or rollback).
